key_terms.لَلْمُتَلَوِّمِ: for the one who lags behind/hesitates
key_terms.لَلْمُقْتَحِمِ: for the one who rushes/enters boldly

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the metaphor of lizards in Imam Ali's sermon at Siffin?
ai.summary: In the context of the Battle of Siffin, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) critiques the Kufans' passive indecision, using the metaphor of lizards rustling in the wind to illustrate their lack of decisive action. He emphasizes that salvation belongs to those who boldly seize the path (al-muqtahim), while destruction awaits those who merely lament their inaction (al-mutallem), highlighting the Shia principle that faith requires active struggle rather than mere contemplation.
